more.question: N5
more.good_when: A maintainer finds a test, named for its case, for every case that the docstrings promise, so a break in any of them shows which promise broke: a credit line whose amount reaches minus a billion is refused just as one reaching plus a billion is (today only the positive end of the amount and of the quantity is tested); an invoice rendered with a currency other than EUR shows that currency on every row; the subtotal of no line is a Decimal zero; and a rate such as `19%%` is refused like any other rate that isn't a percent. And each test of reading the rows (such as the limits of the price and the quantity, a quantity that isn't whole, a row of two fields) names which of the command's cases it supports, as about half of them already do, so that a failing one points to what accounting would see go wrong.

more.question: N7
more.good_when: Breaking any behavior that accounting or a caller of the package relies on makes a test fail. Today each of these breaks passes every test unseen: the amount stops being refused at minus a billion, so a mistyped credit line of a huge negative amount would print; a quantity typed in non-ASCII digits, such as full-width `３`, is taken as 3 when the code means to refuse it; render prints EUR whatever currency its caller asks for; the `%` of the rate is stripped however often it's written, so `--rate 19%%` prints an invoice; the subtotal of no line comes back as a plain integer 0 in place of a Decimal; and a new row of text inside a quoted cell given to parse_lines keeps or loses its carriage return without any test noticing.
